rule: กำ 'to close the hand' takes almost no compounds, and none of the 18 queued here. Its real compounds are already filed and they look alike: กำปั้น and กำมือ carry the etymology กำ + X outright, and กำหมัด is glossed with กำ itself. Everything left is a different word that merely begins with the syllable. Thai's กำ- initial vocabulary is dominated by the Khmer กំ- prefix and by แผลง alteration, and the etymologies say so one by one: กำจร ← ขจร, กำจัด ← ขจัด (Khmer កំចាត់), กำราบ ← กราบ (Khmer កំរាប), กำเดา ← เขดา (Khmer ក្ដៅ), กำไร ← ไกร. Others are outright borrowings (กำปั่น from Malay kapal, กำยาน from kemenyan, ระกำ from Malay), one is a single inherited etymon (กำพร้า < Proto-Tai *ɡm̩.raːꟲ), one is a respelling of another word (กำโชก = กรรโชก), and one is a place name (กำปัง, tambon in Non Thai district). The rule for this head is therefore a NEGATIVE one: a กำ- word belongs to this head only where a source writes กำ + X or the gloss names the hand. Nothing else does.

notes.h2: 2026-09-06 — เห, กำ, กล · and 637 compounds filed by a method the brief disowns

กำเดา ← เขดา (Khmer ក្ដៅ), กำไร ← ไกร. Add outright borrowings (กำปั่น < Malay *kapal*

notes.text:
**A third marker, worth adding to the brief:** `แผลงมาจาก X` — "altered from X". It means
the whole word is a transformation of one other word, and it is decisive for false-split.
It caught five here on its own.

notes.h2: 2026-09-06 — เห, กำ, กล · and 637 compounds filed by a method the brief disowns
notes.text:
**And read the BASE word, not just the compound.** กำสรวล has no etymology of its own. Its
base สรวล does, and it ends `แผลงเป็นเขมร សំរួល` — the Khmer alteration *is* this form.
The evidence was one lookup away and would have been missed by checking the compound only.

notes.h2: 2026-09-06 — เห, กำ, กล · and 637 compounds filed by a method the brief disowns
notes.text:
**Unsure:** six with no etymology anywhere — กำเกียง, กำกับ, กำด้น, กำยำ, กำดัด, กำกวม.
Tagged `standard`, not `verified`. The argument is the pattern their four sourced siblings
demonstrate on this very head, plus the fact that no sense of "close the hand" reaches
"ambiguous", "nape of the neck" or "adolescent". It is a pattern argument, not a source.
กำกับ is the one I would most want a second opinion on.
